speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash on your trunk and extremities, and did it start after the fever and other symptoms began? Also, have you noticed any sensitivity to sunlight or taken any new medications recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see, the facial rash sparing the perioral area is a key detail. Does the rash on your trunk and extremities consist of discrete, flat, pink spots that have not spread to your palms or soles?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text: The facial rash sparing the perioral area, often described as "slapped cheek," combined with the subsequent lacy, reticular rash on the trunk and extremities is classic for Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease). DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum
